warmup.text: Last day of the week. A playful poem with a trick hidden inside it, a little like Praiseworthy's pig. Listen for how a friendly tone can hide what someone really wants.

words.text: Explain aud and or in your own words, and tell why writers use phrases that tell where. In the game, weigh the last six words of the week. Two are fool's gold.

reading.text: Read Chapter 3: a letter home, and a ship in trouble. Watch Captain Swain's choice. Then trace the whole week: the problem, the obstacle, and the hard choice. What is at stake now?

assignment.text: Three questions, the last one about all three chapters. Then submit your adventure plan: hero, problem, setting and stakes. Copy your work and paste it into Canvas.

a big idea about life that a story shows

audible: The word means can be heard.

game.title: The Assayer's Scale
game.sub: This week's word game · 6 words today
game.look: An assayer tested gold in the Gold Rush, to tell real gold from fool's gold. Here you test words. A word with aud (hear) goes on the HEAR pan. A word with or (speak) goes on the SPEAK pan. A word that only looks like one is fool's gold.

do: Read the word on the nugget.
Think about what it means.
Tap HEAR, SPEAK, or Fool's gold.
Tap Next word.
how.why: A root only helps if it is really there. Testing the meaning keeps you from being fooled.

game.doneLine: Every word this week is weighed. Well done.

nuggets.why: audio + visual: something you hear and see.
No root here. Odor is a Latin word for smell.
aud + itorium: a big room for hearing a show.
No root here. Ordinary comes from a Latin word for order, a row.
nuggets.miss: Does ordinary have to do with speaking?

nuggets.why: or + atory: the skill of giving speeches.

art.title: Becalmed off Halfway Rock
art.alt: A painting of sailing ships sitting still on a glassy sea at dawn, with a small rock island between them and a man rowing a little boat.
art.look: Fitz Henry Lane painted this calm in 1860 near Halfway Rock, off the coast of Massachusetts. Not a breath of wind fills the sails. In Chapter 3, a square-rigger sits like this near the equator for a week, far from here.

virtue.name: loyalty
virtue.title: The most loyal moment this week
virtue.intro: Look back at Chapters 1 to 3. Tap the moment you think shows loyalty the most.

options.t: Jack picks the coal bunkers to stay with his partner (Chapter 1).
Praiseworthy gives Jack the credit for the coal-dust trick (Chapter 2).
In his letter home, Jack writes that Praiseworthy never takes credit for himself (Chapter 3).
